Let \(q=3^r\), and let \(\chi\) be the quadratic character of \(\mathbb F_q\), with \(\chi(0)=0\).

Since \(L\cap F=0\), every \(L\) is the graph of a linear map \(S:E\to F\). The Lagrangian condition says \(S\) is symmetric. The condition \(\jmath(L)=L\) forces \(S\) to commute with the sign matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1)\), so, after using the given constraints,
\[
S=\begin{pmatrix}
1&0&a&0\\
0&c&0&0\\
a&0&b&0\\
0&0&0&1
\end{pmatrix},
\]
where
\[
a=s_{13},\qquad b=s_{33},\qquad c=s_{22}.
\]
The equation \(s_{13}^2=A_L+B_L\) becomes
\[
a^2=b+c+2a.
\]
Since the field has characteristic \(3\), this gives
\[
c=a^2+a-b.
\]

Now fix \(t\in\mathbb F_q\). For \(x\in E\), the \(E\)-part of \(\rho_t(x+Sx)\) vanishes for some nonzero \(x\) exactly when
\[
v_t^{T}Sv_t=0.
\]
Here
\[
v_t=(1,t,t^2,t^3),
\]
so
\[
v_t^{T}Sv_t
=t^6+b t^4+(a^2-b)t^2+1.
\]
Thus the condition \(\rho_t(L)\cap F=0\) for every \(t\) is equivalent to
\[
t^6+b t^4+(a^2-b)t^2+1\neq 0
\qquad\forall t\in\mathbb F_q.
\]

Put \(z=t^2\). Then \(z\) ranges over the nonzero squares, plus \(0\), and the value at \(z=0\) is \(1\), so only nonzero squares matter. Define
\[
h_{a,b}(z)=z^3+bz^2+(a^2-b)z+1.
\]
We must count pairs \((a,b)\in\mathbb F_q^2\) for which \(h_{a,b}\) has no nonzero square root.

For \(z=1\),
\[
h_{a,b}(1)=a^2-1,
\]
so \(z=1\) is a root exactly when \(a=\pm1\). For \(z\neq1\), the equation \(h_{a,b}(z)=0\) determines \(b\) uniquely:
\[
b=-\frac{z^3+a^2z+1}{z^2-z}.
\]

By inclusion-exclusion over the possible square roots of the cubic, the count is
\[
M_r=q^2-N_1+N_2-N_3,
\]
where \(N_k\) counts unordered \(k\)-subsets of nonzero squares that occur as roots, weighted by the number of \(a\)'s with the required value of \(a^2\).

First,
\[
N_1=2q+q\left(\frac{q-1}{2}-1\right)=\frac{q(q+1)}2.
\]

For two distinct nonzero squares \(z,w\), the third root is forced to be
\[
-\frac1{zw}.
\]
A direct coefficient comparison gives
\[
a^2=zw-z-w-\frac1z-\frac1w+\frac1{zw}.
\]
The resulting quadratic-character sum over unordered pairs of distinct nonzero squares is
\[
\sum_{\{z,w\}}\chi\!\left(zw-z-w-\frac1z-\frac1w+\frac1{zw}\right)
=
\begin{cases}
0,&r\text{ odd},\\
q,&r\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
\]
Hence the weighted number of unordered square-root pairs is
\[
U=
\frac{(q-1)(q-3)}8+
\begin{cases}
0,&r\text{ odd},\\
q,&r\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
\]

If \(r\) is odd, then \(-1\) is nonsquare, so a cubic with two square roots has nonsquare third root. Therefore
\[
M_r=q^2-\frac{q(q+1)}2+U
=\frac{(q-1)(5q-3)}8.
\]

If \(r\) is even, then \(-1\) is square, so whenever two roots are nonzero squares, the third root is also a nonzero square. Each such cubic is counted three times by unordered pairs but contributes \(2\) in inclusion-exclusion, so the correction is \(\frac23U\). Thus
\[
M_r=q^2-\frac{q(q+1)}2+\frac23U
=\frac{7q^2-2q+3}{12}.
\]

Therefore, with \(q=3^r\),
\[
\boxed{
M_r=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{(q-1)(5q-3)}8,& r\ \text{odd},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{7q^2-2q+3}{12},& r\ \text{even}.
\end{cases}}
\]
